EXPL.Prop2_1.frag.special_j_values.content: For a field K of characteristic zero and t != 0, 1: legendreJ t = 1728 iff t in {-1, 2, 1/2}; legendreJ t = 2^2 73^3 3^-4 iff t in {9, -8, 9/8, -1/8, 8/9, 1/9}; legendreJ t = 2^14 31^3 5^-3 iff t is a root of t^2 - 125t + 125, t^2 + 123t + 1 or 125t^2 - 125t + 1; legendreJ t = 0 iff t^2 - t + 1 = 0. Over Q no t != 0, 1 has j = 2^14 31^3 5^-3 or j = 0 (no rational square equals 5; t^2 - t + 1 > 0). legendreJ (1/9) = 2^2 73^3 3^-4 and legendreJ (1/2) = 1728.
explicit_hypotheses: K a field of characteristic zero, t in K, t != 0, t != 1 (for the rational statements t in Q)
EXPL.Prop2_1.frag.special_j_values.conclusion: The solution sets listed in content.
external_dependencies: Explicit estimates in IUT (Mochizuki, Fesenko, Hoshi, Minamide, Porowski): Proposition 2.1, page 21, the list of the four values (read); CanLift: Proposition 2.7 (not read)
EXPL.Prop2_1.frag.special_j_values.covers: Page 21, Proposition 2.1: the four values 2^14 31^3 5^-3, 2^2 73^3 3^-4, 1728 and 0 of j(E), and for each value the points of the Legendre lambda-line with that j-invariant. IUT IV page 43 (proof of Corollary 2.2 (ii)) says only that there are 'four possibilities' ([CanLift], Proposition 2.7) and puts the finite set of points corresponding to them into Exc_d.
EXPL.Prop2_1.frag.special_j_values.not_covered: That the j-invariant of a curve without an F-core is one of the four values (Proposition 2.1 itself, from [Sijs] Table 4 and [CanLift], Proposition 2.7), the notion of F-core, and the rest of IUT IV Corollary 2.2 (ii). The points of the lambda-line over the four values are printed neither on page 21 nor on IUT IV page 43; they are computed here from the printed values. Because the points checked here are not printed, this record is counted as a model test.
ambiguities: IUT IV does not list the four values; they are taken from Explicit estimates, Proposition 2.1. Proved here: legendreJ (1/9) = 2^2 73^3 3^-4 (legendreJ_one_ninth) and the six-point solution set of that value (legendreJ_eq_73_iff); so the point 1/9 of the triple 1 + 8 = 9 has this j-value. That this value is the j-invariant of a curve without an F-core (Explicit estimates, Proposition 2.1; [CanLift], Proposition 2.7) and that such points are excluded into Exc_d (IUT IV page 43) are statements of the papers, not proved here.

GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.content: Arithmetic divisors on a number field F: finite formal sums of valuations with integer coefficients at nonarchimedean and real coefficients at archimedean valuations, forming the group ADiv(F). The principal arithmetic divisor of f in F is ADiv(f) = sum over nonarchimedean v of ord_v(f) v minus sum over archimedean v of [F_v : R] log|f|_v v; these form the subgroup APrc(F). The degree map deg_F is defined on ADiv(F)/APrc(F), which is isomorphic to APic(Spec O_F) ([Szp], Proposition 1.1), by the weights log(q_v) at nonarchimedean and 1 at archimedean valuations, and the normalized degree (1/[F : Q]) deg_F is invariant under finite extension for arithmetic line bundles.
explicit_hypotheses: f a nonzero element of F
GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.conclusion: deg_F is a homomorphism on ADiv(F)/APrc(F), so it vanishes on principal arithmetic divisors; the normalized degree of an arithmetic line bundle is invariant under restriction to a finite extension.
obligations: The isomorphism ADiv(F)/APrc(F) = APic(Spec O_F) and arithmetic line bundles are not formalized; the principal divisor and the vanishing of the degree on it are (GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.frag.principal, GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.frag.degF_principal).

GENELL.Def1_2.frag.heightNF_algebraMap.content: For number fields K, L with an algebra map K -> L and y in K, the normalized height heightNF (Mathlib's Height.logHeight1 divided by the degree over Q) of y read in L equals that of y read in K. Proof: logHeight1 y is the degree deg_K of the polar divisor of y (coefficient max(0, -ord_v y) at finite places, [K_v : R] log+ |y|_v at archimedean places); its pull-back along degPbPullback is the polar divisor of y in L; deg_L of a pull-back is [L : K] deg_K. The same holds for y mapped by any ring homomorphism K -> L (htExt_heightNF_ringHom), in particular by an isomorphism.
explicit_hypotheses: K, L number fields with an algebra map K -> L
GENELL.Def1_2.frag.heightNF_algebraMap.conclusion: heightNF L (algebraMap K L y) = heightNF K y; equivalently Height.logHeight1 (algebraMap K L y) = [L : K] Height.logHeight1 y.
GENELL.Def1_2.frag.heightNF_algebraMap.covers: GenEll page 4: the normalized degree is invariant under finite extension, so that ht(x) = deg_F(x_F^* M) may be computed through any morphism x_F : Spec(O_F) -> X giving rise to x; Definition 1.2 (i), page 5: ht is a function on X(Qbar). GENELL.Def1_5.content: (i) A point x in X(F), [F : Q] finite, has a well-defined minimal field of definition F_min in F, from the scheme-theoretic image of Spec(F) -> X. (ii) Reduced effective Cartier divisors. (iii) For x in X(F) with F a minimal field of definition of x, the different ideal of F gives an effective arithmetic divisor delta_x supported at the finite places, and log-diff_X(x) = deg_F(delta_x) (normalized degree) defines the log-different function on X(Qbar). (iv) For an effective Cartier divisor D of X, U_X = X \ D and x in U_X(F) with F a minimal field of definition, the pull-back D_x of D to Spec(O_F), the conductor f_x^D = (D_x)_red, and log-cond_D(x) = deg_F(f_x^D) defines the log-conductor function on U_X(Qbar).
explicit_hypotheses: X a normal scheme, proper and flat over Spec(Z) (page 3)
D an effective Cartier divisor of X (for (iv))
GENELL.Def1_5.conclusion: Definitions: the minimal field of definition of a point, the log-different function on X(Qbar) and the log-conductor function on U_X(Qbar), both evaluated at the minimal field of definition.
obligations: (iii) and (iv) are formalized for X = P^1 over Z and D = {0, 1, infinity}, as the definitions logDiffNF and logCondNF of IUT.Applications.VojtaNumberField, evaluated at a field generated by the point; (ii) and general X, D are not formalized. The fragments record how the values change when the point is read in a larger field; the page does not state these changes.

GENELL.Def1_5.frag.logCondNF_extension.content: For number fields K -> L, y in K \ {0, 1} and S the finite set of primes of K at which y meets {0, 1, infinity}: [L : Q] (log-cond_K(y) - log-cond_L(y)) = sum over v in S and primes w of L over v of (e(w|v) - 1) log q_w. Hence log-cond_L(y) <= log-cond_K(y), with equality when every prime of L at which y meets the boundary is unramified over K.
explicit_hypotheses: K, L number fields with an algebra map K -> L
y in K, y != 0, y != 1 (or, for the identity, a finite set S equal to the set of primes where y meets the boundary)
for the equality: e(w|v) = 1 at every prime w of L at which y meets the boundary
GENELL.Def1_5.frag.logCondNF_extension.covers: Page 8, Definition 1.5 (iv): log-cond_D(x) is the normalized degree of the reduced divisor (D_x)_red on Spec O_F for a minimal field of definition F; the theorems show how the value read in a larger field differs (it drops under ramification at the conductor).

GENELL.Def1_5.frag.minimal_field_equival.content: The registered statement VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost d, which reads each point on its minimal field of definition, is equivalent with the same constants to htExtDegreeAtMostAnyFieldStatement d, which reads each point x in any number field F of degree at most d containing it. DIM.Thm.content: There are computable functions eta, c : N x (0, 1) x N -> (0, 1) and C : N x (0, 1) x N -> R such that, for a finite set Sigma of places of Q and a function A : R x (0, 1) -> R: if every P in K_Sigma(eta(d, eps, |Sigma|)) with [Q(P) : Q] <= d satisfies h(P) <= (1 + eps)(cond_{[0]+[1]+[inf]}(P) + d(P)) + A(d, eps) for all (d, eps), then every P in P^1(Qbar) \ {0, 1, inf} with [Q(P) : Q] <= d satisfies h(P) <= (1 + eps)(cond_{[0]+[1]+[inf]}(P) + d(P)) + 2 A(150 d eps^-2, c(d, eps, |Sigma|)) + C(d, eps, |Sigma|).
explicit_hypotheses: Sigma a finite set of places of Q
A : R x (0, 1) -> R a function
K_Sigma(eta) the compactly bounded subset of page 2, supported at Sigma
DIM.Thm.conclusion: An effective reduction of the bounded degree inequality on P^1 minus three points to compactly bounded subsets.
obligations: Not formalized. The fragment checks one step of the proof (page 9): a point of the Fermat curve over a given point of P^1 and the degree of its field. The heights on C_n of displays (7) and (8), the Belyi maps and the effective Nullstellensatz are not formalized.

LANA.Sec10.content: Section 10.1: the eta algorithm (steps 1 to 9) constructs, from a BPS and a fixed isomorphism to the Theta-BPS of a Hodge theater, an action of N on the volume container of the log-shell; its anabelian steps are described without construction. Section 10.2: R^ss is the set of adelic measurable subsets of the container modulo equal volume; a subset S of the log-shell gives an isomorphism eta^anab_S from R^val to R^ss sending the pilot to the class of the image of S under 1 in N; the q-BPS gives eta^q, sending the pilot to the class of {q_v O_v}. The main goal is to show that there is some suitable S with eta^q = eta^anab_S. The introduction of section 10 states the authors' belief that a solution of this problem would give Corollary 3.12; section 11.5 states that the project has no proof of the equality.
explicit_hypotheses: a BPS with a fixed isomorphism to the Theta-BPS of a Hodge theater (section 10.1)

LANA.Sec5.content: The report replaces the prime-strips of IUT by basic prime strips (BPS). An etale BPS is a family, over the places, of topological groups isomorphic to the local Galois groups; an etale-unit BPS is a family of mono-analytic GM-data with compact structure, isomorphic to the reference data; a value-group BPS is a one-dimensional oriented real vector space with nonzero local pilots whose sum over the bad places is nonzero, with product formula the kernel of the map from the direct sum of copies of R over the places; isomorphisms are families of isomorphisms, resp. linear isomorphisms matching the local pilots. Remark: when the product formula is fixed, a value-group BPS is given by a pointed oriented real line with a negative pilot. A BPS is a pair of an etale-unit BPS and a value-group BPS. Lemma (section 5.1.3): two BPS are isomorphic if and only if their product formulas agree.
explicit_hypotheses: the places of the initial Theta-data and the bad places (sections 3 and 4 of the report)
LANA.Sec5.conclusion: Definitions of BPS and their isomorphisms, and the lemma that two BPS are isomorphic exactly when their product formulas agree.
obligations: The reference objects (the local Galois groups, the monoids with their compact structures) are not constructed; the fragments take them as parameters and are model tests on the report's simplified objects, not on the prime-strips of IUT I to IV.
ambiguities: Section 5.2.3 gives the q-pilot value-group BPS with positive local pilots in C = R, while the remark of section 5.1.2 calls the pilot negative; the report does not say how the two agree.

LANA.Sec9.content: The report quotes the properties (IPL), (SHE) and (APT) from IUT III, Remark 3.11.1, and translates (IPL): the intermediate BPS in the construction of the output region of Theorem 3.11 is linked by the full poly-isomorphism to the q-pilot BPS.
